questions.stem: Two angles lie on a straight line. If one of them is $65°$, find the other.
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to $180°$, so the other angle is $180° - 65° = 115°$. Such a pair is described as supplementary.

distractorRationale.a: Subtracted from 90°, treating the angles as complementary
distractorRationale.c: Doubled 65 instead of subtracting from 180
distractorRationale.d: Subtracted from 360°, which applies to angles at a point

questions.stem: What is the sum of all the angles at a point?
questions.explanation: The angles at a point together make one complete revolution, and a full turn is $360°$. This is different from angles on a straight line, which make only half a turn.

distractorRationale.a: This is a right angle, a quarter turn
distractorRationale.b: This is the sum of angles on a straight line, a half turn
distractorRationale.c: This is three right angles, not a full turn

questions.stem: When two straight lines cross, the vertically opposite angles formed are:
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are always equal, and this holds whether or not any lines are parallel. It follows from the straight-line rule: each of the two angles is $180°$ minus the same adjacent angle.

distractorRationale.b: Adjacent angles at the crossing are supplementary, not vertically opposite ones
distractorRationale.c: Complementary angles add to 90°, which is not implied here
distractorRationale.d: True only in the special case where the lines are perpendicular

questions.stem: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. One of the angles formed is $70°$. What is the size of the corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so the corresponding angle is also $70°$. They form the familiar F shape, sitting in matching positions at the two intersections.

distractorRationale.d: Doubled the given angle

questions.stem: Two co-interior angles are formed when a transversal cuts a pair of parallel lines. If one of them is $115°$, find the other.
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary, so they add to $180°$. The other angle is $180° - 115° = 65°$. This is the one parallel-line pair that is not equal.

distractorRationale.c: Subtracted from 190 by arithmetic slip
distractorRationale.d: Subtracted from 360°

questions.stem: Three angles $x$, $2x$ and $3x$ lie on a straight line. Find the value of $x$ in degrees. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add to $180°$, so $x + 2x + 3x = 180$, giving $6x = 180$ and $x = 30$. The three angles are then $30°$, $60°$ and $90°$, which do add to $180°$.

questions.stem: Alternate angles formed when a transversal cuts two parallel lines are:
questions.explanation: Alternate angles lie on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines, forming a Z shape. On parallel lines they are equal. Only co-interior angles are supplementary.

distractorRationale.c: Complementary angles add to 90° and are not a parallel-line relationship
distractorRationale.d: No fixed ratio arises from parallel lines

questions.stem: Four angles at a point are $90°$, $x$, $2x$ and $30°$. Find the value of $x$.
questions.explanation: Angles at a point add to $360°$, so $90 + x + 2x + 30 = 360$. That gives $3x = 240$ and $x = 80°$. The four angles are then $90°$, $80°$, $160°$ and $30°$.

distractorRationale.a: Used 180° for the total instead of 360°
distractorRationale.b: Divided 240 by 4 instead of 3
distractorRationale.d: Gave $2x$ rather than $x$

questions.stem: Two angles are supplementary. One of them is $30°$ more than twice the other. Find the larger angle.
questions.explanation: Let the smaller angle be $x$, so the other is $2x + 30$. Supplementary means $x + 2x + 30 = 180$, giving $3x = 150$ and $x = 50$. The larger angle is $2(50) + 30 = 130°$, and $50 + 130 = 180$ as required.

distractorRationale.a: This is the smaller angle, not the larger one
distractorRationale.b: Gave $2x$ but forgot to add the 30
distractorRationale.d: Solved $3x = 150$ and then read 150 as the answer

questions.stem: Two complementary angles are in the ratio $2 : 3$. Find the larger angle.
questions.explanation: Complementary angles add to $90°$. With $2 + 3 = 5$ parts, one part is $90 \div 5 = 18°$. The larger angle has 3 parts, so it is $3 \times 18 = 54°$.

distractorRationale.a: This is the smaller angle, 2 parts
distractorRationale.c: Used 180° as the total instead of 90°, then took 2 parts
distractorRationale.d: Used 180° as the total and took 3 parts
